what_it_is: AI security platform for discovery, posture, red teaming, guardrails and agent control.
identity_note: Formerly AppSOC. Many pages still say AppSOC and the old DevSecOps orchestration platform page remains live.

1.reason: AI Discovery inventories models, agents and MCP servers. AI-SPM finds MLOps misconfigs. Workforce control finds Shadow AI.
1.evidence: Discovers models, agents, MCP servers, notebooks, and more
1.verify_note: AI Discovery page confirms Databricks, Azure and AWS integration, MLOps pipeline visibility and model supply chain risk. Workforce AI Usage Control page confirms shadow AI.

2.reason: MCP Security Gateway and Agent Mission Control check tool calls before execution, with sandboxing and kill switches.
2.evidence: Hypervisor-grade sandboxing with privilege tiers. Emergency kill switches for single agents or groups
2.verify_note: Agent Mission Control page confirms sandboxing and kill switches. MCP Security Gateway page and Copilot Studio integration page both exist.

3.reason: Agent Mission Control contains anomalies at runtime. Guardrails module sends issues to Jira and ServiceNow.
3.evidence: Seamless integration with Jira, ServiceNow, Teams and other operational tools
3.verify_note: Governance page names only SOC and IR workflows. Jira and ServiceNow appear on the guardrails page, so the URL moves there. Status unchanged.

4.reason: Intelligent AI Guardrails inspect prompts and responses via API or proxy and scan output for malicious code.
4.evidence: Stops prompt injection and jailbreak attacks. Scans responses for malware or malicious code
4.verify_note: Guardrails page says responses are scanned for malware or malicious code, so 4.3 rises to yes.

5.reason: AI Governance maps to ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, OWASP LLM. AI Discovery manages the AI BOM.
5.evidence: Aligns with ISO 42001, HIPAA, NIST AI RMF, OWASP Top 10 for LLMs
5.verify_note: Governance page confirms ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF and OWASP LLM alignment. AI Discovery page confirms AI BOM management.

6.reason: AI Security Testing runs automated red teaming against models and agents. No CI/CD red teaming detail found.
6.evidence: Automate model & agent scanning, Red Teaming, and risk & trust validation
6.verify_note: Testing page confirms automated red teaming of models and agents. CI/CD red teaming search found only an AppSOC DevSecOps blog, 6.3 stays partial.

7.reason: Agent Identity & Access gives each agent a cryptographic identity and intent-based least-privilege access to MCP tools.
7.evidence: Assign every AI agent a decentralized cryptographic identity bound to its owner, purpose, permissions, and operating scope
7.verify_note: Identity page confirms DIDs, intent-based least privilege and MCP tool controls. 7.3 stays partial on OAuth delegation and credential scope control, not the glossary.

8.reason: Static and dynamic model scanning finds malware in models. Dataset and AI code scanning are narrower.
8.evidence: Detects embedded malware, vulnerabilities, and weaknesses. Scans notebooks for vulnerable libraries
8.verify_note: Testing page confirms embedded malware detection in models and notebook library scans. Dataset work is lineage only, 8.2 stays partial.

notes: Rebranded from AppSOC. Legacy AppSOC ASPM aggregates 130+ SAST, SCA and DAST tools, which a reviewer may count toward 8.3. AI Discovery tracks dataset lineage, but no training-data PII or poisoning scan was found. Newer products: Agent Mission Control, Agentic Endpoint Security, Workforce AI Usage Control. A July 2026 Gartner note quotes Agent Mission Control. NHI support appears only on a glossary page (short-lived per-agent identities), so 7.3 is partial. 6.3 CI/CD red teaming: two searches found nothing.
